finishes.headline: Three kinds of stain. Here's the honest difference.

transparent.name: Transparent / toner
transparent.look: Almost all grain. A light tint.
transparent.bestFor: New or nice wood you want to show off. Needs the most frequent recoats.

semi-transparent.name: Semi-transparent
semi-transparent.bestFor: Most deck floors. Fades instead of peeling, so recoats are easy.

solid.name: Solid color
solid.look: Even color, like paint. Texture only.
solid.bestFor: Railings, fences and patched or mismatched wood. Can peel on floors.

finishes.footnote: Prices shown are sample rates for a deck in good shape; weathered and peeling decks cost more. [Read: semi-transparent vs. solid](/learn/semi-transparent-vs-solid-deck-stain/)

products.headline: We use EXPERT™ Stain & Seal.
paragraphs: [EXPERT Stain & Seal](source:expertStainSeal) is an oil-based, penetrating stain for decks, fences and exterior wood, made in transparent, semi-transparent and semi-solid finishes. Penetrating oil soaks into the wood instead of forming a film on top, which is the kind of finish the U.S. Forest Products Lab recommends for decks{cite:usdaFinishes}.

For log homes we use [EXPERT Log & Timber Oil](source:supplierLogOil), and [EXPERT Clean & Bright](source:expertCleanBright) for the wash and brightener. EXPERT reports it was the [first oil-based wood stain to earn GREENWISE® certification](source:expertGreenwise).
We buy it through **Stain & Seal Supply** as a [Pro Partner](source:supplierProPartner), so we get pro-grade product and training.

faq.headline: What homeowners ask us most
faq.intro: Straight answers, with links to the experts where it matters. More in our [Learn](/learn/) section.

items.q: How much does deck staining cost in {city}?
items.a: Nationally, Angi puts a typical job at $550–$1,250, about $850 on average, or roughly $2 to $4 per square foot ([Angi, 2026](source:angi)). Your price depends on size, railings, stairs and how much prep the wood needs. Our price calculator gives you a range in about a minute.

items.q: How often does a deck need to be restained?
items.a: Most sources say every two to three years for a deck floor ([Angi](source:angi)). The U.S. Forest Products Lab gives semi-transparent stain about 2–3 years on new smooth decking and 3–6 years on weathered wood ([USDA FPL](source:usdaSouth)). Shade, sun and use change that.

items.q: When is the best time of year to stain a deck in {city}?
items.a: {bestMonths}. {driestMonth} is the driest month on average here, and {fewestRainDays} have the fewest rainy days ([NOAA normals](source:climate)). Stain needs dry wood and a few dry days.

The experts disagree. The U.S. Forest Products Lab says film finishes like solid stain tend to peel on decks ([USDA FPL](source:usdaFinishes)). Consumer Reports says solid scores best in their testing ([via KOMO](source:consumerReports)). We usually suggest semi-transparent on floors and solid on railings, if you want solid.
Not the way most people mean it. High pressure can strip wood fibers off the surface ([USDA FPL](source:usdaFinishes)). We use cleaners and low pressure, then a brightener.

items.q: Can you give me a price from photos?
items.a: Yes. That's how most of our estimates start. Upload up to five photos, including one wide shot of the whole deck, and we'll send a price range. We confirm it in person or by video before we start.

In {licenseCounty}, {stateName} requires a Home Improvement license for residential jobs from $3,000 to $24,999 ([TN.gov](source:tnHomeImprovement)). Our license and insurance are listed at the bottom of every page.

items.q: Do I need to be home?
items.a: No. We just need access to the deck, a water spigot, and pets kept inside. We'll text you when we start, when we finish each day, and before we leave.

infoBoxes.title: How does the cleaning preview work?
infoBoxes.text: It simulates what a wash and brightener do: gray weathering and mildew blotches even out to fresh wood, while the grain, board gaps and shadows stay. It's a preview, not a promise. Boards that are cracked or soft won't come back with cleaning alone, and we'll tell you if yours need replacing.

infoBoxes.title: Why does it look different from the can?
infoBoxes.text: Stain soaks into wood, so the wood's own color shows through, especially on semi-transparent. Old gray wood, new yellow pine and red cedar all take the same stain differently. This tool keeps your wood's grain and light and dark spots, so it's closer to real than a color chip.

infoBoxes.title: Is my photo private?
infoBoxes.text: Yes. The image stays on your device while you work. It's only sent to us if you fill in the form to get the full-size image. See our [privacy page](/privacy/).

infoBoxes.title: Tips for a good photo
infoBoxes.text: Shoot in daylight but not in harsh noon sun. Stand back far enough to get the whole deck. Sweep the leaves off first if you can. Wet boards look darker, so wait until it's dry.

services.name: Deck Staining
services.photoAlt: Freshly stained hardwood deck boards seen from above
services.seoDescription: Professional deck staining in {city}: low-pressure wash, brightener, two coats brushed in by hand. Sample pricing from {semiFrom}/sq ft. Free photo estimates.
services.lede: We wash, we brighten, we stain. Most decks take two days.
services.intro: Most decks we see around {city} aren't ruined. They're gray, a little rough, maybe green on the shady side. Under that is good wood that just needs the right prep and a stain that soaks in.

steps.title: Protect
steps.text: Cover plants, siding and anything we don't want stain on. Move furniture and grills (and put them back).

steps.title: Wash
steps.text: Low-pressure wash with a cleaner that lifts gray and mildew. No blasting soft wood.

steps.title: Brighten
steps.text: Brightener evens out the color and opens the grain so stain soaks in evenly.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: We let it dry. Usually overnight at least, longer in shade. This is the step most people rush.

steps.title: Stain
steps.text: Penetrating stain, applied and back-brushed board by board. Rails and spindles by hand.

steps.title: Walk-through
steps.text: We walk it with you, touch up anything you point out, and leave care instructions.

faq.q: How long until we can use the deck?
faq.a: Light foot traffic usually the next day. Furniture back in 24–48 hours depending on the product and weather. We'll tell you for your exact stain.

faq.q: Do you sand?
faq.a: Only where it helps: raised grain, rough patches, splinters. Sanding a whole deck smooth can actually keep stain from soaking in, so we don't do it by default.

faq.q: What if it rains?
faq.a: We watch the forecast closely and reschedule if needed. If rain surprises us before the stain sets, we come back and fix it. That's on us.

services.name: Deck Cleaning & Restoration
services.photoAlt: Gray, weathered deck boards that need cleaning
services.seoTitle: Deck Cleaning & Restoration in {city} — Wash, Strip, Brighten, Sand | {short}
services.seoDescription: Deck restoration in {city}: remove peeling stain, clean mildew, brighten gray wood and sand rough boards — then seal it right. Photo estimates.
services.lede: Gray, green or peeling? That deck can come back.
services.intro: Restoration is everything that happens before the stain goes on. It's the difference between a finish that lasts and one that peels by next summer.

steps.title: Wash
steps.text: For faded and mildewed decks: a cleaner that kills the green and lifts the gray, rinsed at low pressure.

steps.title: Strip
steps.text: For peeling or failing finish: a stripper that softens the old coat so it rinses off without gouging the wood.

steps.title: Brighten
steps.text: Neutralizes the stripper or cleaner and brings the wood back to an even, fresh color.

steps.title: Sand
steps.text: Spot-sanding for raised grain, splinters and rough board ends.

steps.title: Repair
steps.text: Reset popped nails, swap cracked boards, tighten loose rails. Priced per item, no surprises.

steps.title: Seal
steps.text: Finish with the right stain for your wood and how you use the deck.

faq.q: Why not just pressure-wash it?
faq.a: High pressure tears up soft wood. The U.S. Forest Products Lab warns that power washing can remove wood from the surface. We use cleaners and low pressure instead.

faq.q: How do I know if mine needs stripping?
faq.a: If the old coat is peeling, flaking or blotchy, it needs to come off. If it's just faded and gray, a wash and brightener is usually enough. Photos tell us a lot.

faq.q: Can you fix a few bad boards?
faq.a: Yes. We replace individual boards and note them on the estimate. For structural problems (posts, joists, ledger), we'll tell you and refer you to a deck builder.

services.name: Fence Staining
services.photoAlt: Close-up of cedar fence boards with ivy
services.seoTitle: Fence Staining in {city} — Privacy, Picket & Board Fences | {short}
services.seoDescription: Wood fence staining in {city}. We spray and back-brush both sides so stain soaks in. Bundle with your deck to save on setup.
services.lede: Fences are vertical, so a good stain lasts longer on them than on a deck floor.
services.intro: A wood fence is a lot of square footage, and most of it has never been sealed. Done right once, a fence stays easy to keep up.

steps.title: Clean
steps.text: Wash off gray, mildew and dirt so the stain soaks into wood, not grime.

steps.title: Protect
steps.text: Cover plants, AC units, cars and the neighbor's side if we're only doing yours.

steps.title: Spray & back-brush
steps.text: We spray to cover fast, then brush it in. Spray-only jobs look fine for a season and then fade unevenly.

steps.title: Both sides
steps.text: Priced per side. Ask your neighbor. Many split the cost of the other side.

faq.q: How is fence staining priced?
faq.a: By the linear foot and height, per side. Send a photo and the rough length and we'll give you a range.

faq.q: Can my fence match my deck?
faq.a: Yes, but fences and decks often look different with the same stain because the wood and sun are different. We'll test it first.

services.name: Log Home & Cabin Staining
services.photoAlt: Log cabin with a covered porch and stacked firewood
services.seoTitle: Log Home & Cabin Staining in {city} and the Mountains | {short}
services.seoDescription: Log home and cabin staining around {city}: cleaning, old finish removal, and stain made for logs. {cabinAreas}.
services.lede: Logs move, check and drink stain. They need their own plan.
services.intro: Log walls take more weather than a deck rail and soak up more stain than you'd guess. We clean them, deal with the old finish, and stain them so water runs off instead of in.

steps.title: Inspect
steps.text: Look for soft spots, open checks on the top side of logs, and chinking gaps. We'll show you what we find.

steps.title: Clean
steps.text: Gentle wash for dirt, pollen and mildew. Strip failing finish where needed.

steps.title: Stain
steps.text: A log-home stain applied heavy enough to protect and brushed into checks and end grain.

steps.title: Trim & porches
steps.text: Doors, window trim, porch posts and decks matched to the walls.

faq.q: How often do log homes need restaining?
faq.a: It depends on sun, overhangs and the product. South and west walls wear fastest. We'll look at each side and tell you which ones need it now.

faq.q: Do you do chinking?
faq.a: We handle small chinking repairs as part of a stain job. For a full re-chink we'll refer you to a specialist.

services.name: Pergolas, Porches & Gazebos
services.photoAlt: Stained timber pavilion posts and floor with fall trees behind
services.seoDescription: Staining for pergolas, porches, gazebos, arbors and swing sets in {city}. Hand-brushed posts and beams, matched to your deck.
services.lede: All the posts, beams and slats that a sprayer misses.
services.intro: Pergolas and gazebos have a lot of edges and end grain, and that's where water gets in. We take the time to brush every face, including the tops of beams you can't see from the ground.

steps.title: Overhead work
steps.text: Ladders and staging for beams and rafters. We protect the floor and furniture underneath.

steps.title: End grain first
steps.text: Cut ends soak up water the fastest, so we seal them first and heaviest.

steps.title: Porch floors
steps.text: Covered porch floors get a finish suited to foot traffic and the occasional muddy boot.

steps.title: Match the deck
steps.text: If we're doing the deck too, we'll match or coordinate colors.

faq.q: Can you stain a cedar swing set or playset?
faq.a: Yes. We use a product suited to it and let it cure properly before the kids are back on it.

faq.q: My porch floor is painted. Can you stain it?
faq.a: Sometimes. Tongue-and-groove porch floors are often meant to be painted. We'll tell you honestly which finish fits.

steps.text: Plan customers get first pick of fall dates, our busiest season.

steps.title: Warranty stays active
steps.text: Staying on schedule keeps your warranty going.

faq.q: What's the difference between a maintenance coat and a full job?
faq.a: A full job may include stripping, heavy cleaning, brightening and two coats. A maintenance coat is a gentle wash and one fresh coat over finish that's still sound. It's faster and costs much less.

faq.q: Can I cancel?
faq.a: Yes. Yearly plans can be cancelled any time before the next visit is booked. Monthly plans can be cancelled with 30 days' notice.

faq.q: Are these real prices?
faq.a: On this demo site they are sample prices. Each Pro Partner sets their own in the site settings.

areas.name: Chattanooga
areas.headline: Deck staining in Chattanooga, from North Shore porches to Missionary Ridge decks
areas.lede: Home base. We work every part of the city, and the decks change a lot from one side of the river to the other.
areas.photoAlt: Historic photograph of Chattanooga Valley and the Tennessee River from Lookout Mountain, 1860s

sections.headline: Older homes, older finishes
sections.text: In North Shore, Highland Park, St. Elmo and Riverview, a lot of the porches and back decks have been painted or solid-stained more than once. Layers like that trap water and peel in sheets. Another coat on top won't hold. We strip it back to wood the right way and start the finish over, or we tell you honestly when a board needs replacing first.

sections.headline: Ridge decks get the weather first
sections.text: Up on Missionary Ridge and the bluffs, decks sit high and catch full afternoon sun and wind. The finish on the floor and the top rail goes first. Those decks usually need a maintenance coat sooner than one tucked into a shady backyard downtown.

sections.headline: River-bottom humidity
sections.text: Low ground near the river and creeks stays damp. You'll see green on the north side of the boards and black spots under planters. We wash that out gently, kill the mildew, and let the wood dry before any stain goes on.

woodNotes: Multi-layer paint and solid stain on porches
Sun-baked deck floors on the ridges
Mildew on north-facing and low-lying decks

faq.q: Do you work on the small porches and decks in the older Chattanooga neighborhoods?
faq.a: Yes. Small jobs are welcome. There's a minimum job price, but a 10×12 porch floor is right in our wheelhouse, and those often need stripping more than size.

areas.name: Signal Mountain
areas.headline: Deck staining on Signal Mountain: shade, moss and mildew are the enemy
areas.lede: Signal Mountain sits up on Walden Ridge under thick hardwoods. Beautiful to live with. Hard on a deck.
areas.photoAlt: Wooden deck under hardwood trees beside a stone house

sections.headline: Why mountain decks go green
sections.text: Under a full canopy, the boards stay damp for days after a rain. Leaves pile up in the gaps and hold water against the wood. That's where mildew, algae and moss get started, and why a Signal deck can look worse at three years than a sunny valley deck at five.

sections.headline: What we do differently up here
sections.text: We spend more time on cleaning. We blow out the board gaps, use a mildew wash that's safe for the plants around the deck, and never blast soft wood with high pressure. We also steer most shady decks toward a stain made to resist mildew, and away from thick solid colors that trap moisture.

sections.headline: Log homes and cabins on the mountain
sections.text: There are plenty of log and cedar-sided homes on Signal and Walden. We stain those too. They have their own needs, like checking for gaps in the chinking and dealing with old finish on the logs.

faq.q: How often will my Signal Mountain deck need a recoat?
faq.a: Usually on the shorter end of the range. Shady decks hold moisture and grow mildew faster. A yearly wash plus a maintenance coat every 2 years keeps most of them from ever needing a full strip.

areas.name: Lookout Mountain
areas.headline: Deck staining on Lookout Mountain, on both sides of the state line
areas.lede: The decks up here were built for the view. Many hang off steep lots with long railings and tall stairs.
areas.photoAlt: Wood deck and rail on a cabin overlooking a wooded mountain valley

sections.headline: Built for the view, hard to reach
sections.text: Lookout decks tend to be tall, multi-level and on steep ground. That means more railing, more stairs, and more ladder work than a flat backyard deck. We price railings and stairs separately so you can see exactly where the cost is.

sections.headline: Railings show wear first
sections.text: Top rails and balusters take the sun and rain straight on and are the first thing your guests touch. On view decks we pay extra attention to the vertical parts. A well-done railing makes the whole deck look new.

sections.headline: Tennessee side or Georgia side
sections.text: The mountain crosses the state line, and so do we. Whether your mailbox says Lookout Mountain, TN or Lookout Mountain, GA, the work and the warranty are the same.

woodNotes: Tall, multi-level decks on steep lots
Long runs of railing and stairs
Wind and full sun on the bluff side, deep shade on the back side

faq.q: Can you stain a deck that's 20 feet off the ground?
faq.a: Yes. We set up safely with the right ladders and staging, and we'll tell you up front if a section needs special equipment so there's no surprise on the bill.

areas.name: Red Bank
areas.headline: Deck and porch staining in Red Bank
areas.lede: Red Bank sits between downtown and the foot of Signal Mountain. Lots of mid-century homes with decks that were added later on.

sections.headline: Add-on decks and their quirks
sections.text: Many Red Bank homes got their decks years after the house was built. Some were built well, some were weekend jobs. Before we stain, we check the boards, nails and railings, and point out anything loose. A fresh stain shouldn't hide a problem.

sections.headline: Front porches deserve it too
sections.text: Covered porches don't get rain, but they get foot traffic, and that wears a finish down in a path from the door to the steps. We can stain a porch floor in a day and blend the worn path back in.

sections.headline: Close by, easy to fit in
sections.text: Red Bank is right next to our usual routes. If you're flexible on timing, we can often fit smaller Red Bank jobs in between bigger ones.

woodNotes: Small-yard jobs that fit between bigger ones

faq.q: Is my old deck worth staining or should it be replaced?
faq.a: Send us photos first. If the framing is sound and most boards are solid, cleaning and staining plus a few new boards costs a fraction of a rebuild. If it isn't safe, we'll tell you.

areas.name: Hixson
areas.headline: Deck staining in Hixson, from subdivisions to Chickamauga Lake
areas.lede: Hixson has a bit of everything: family subdivisions, wooded lots off the ridges, and lake houses on Chickamauga Lake.
areas.photoAlt: Deck with wooden railing and chairs looking into green trees

sections.headline: The typical Hixson deck
sections.text: A pressure-treated deck off the back of a two-story, about 12 by 16 to 16 by 20, with a set of stairs to the yard. It's 10 to 20 years old and was stained once, maybe twice. Most of these need a good wash, a brightener and two coats of a semi-transparent. That's our bread and butter.

sections.headline: Lake houses take more care
sections.text: Decks near Chickamauga Lake see damp mornings, sun off the water and more mildew than a deck in town. Docks and boat-house decks are a different animal. Tell us what you've got and we'll tell you honestly what will last.

sections.headline: Fences too
sections.text: A lot of Hixson yards have long privacy fences. If you're getting the deck done, staining the fence the same week saves you a second setup charge.

faq.q: Can you do my deck and fence in the same visit?
faq.a: Yes, and it's cheaper that way. One setup, one cleanup, and matched colors if you want them.

areas.name: Soddy-Daisy
areas.headline: Deck staining in Soddy-Daisy and along the north end of the lake
areas.lede: More land, bigger decks, and plenty of lake homes. Soddy-Daisy jobs tend to be the larger ones on our calendar.
areas.photoAlt: Log cabin home in the woods

sections.headline: Big decks, wraparounds and lake views
sections.text: Out here a deck is often a wraparound, or two levels stepping down a slope toward the water. Big decks reward good prep. One bad wash day shows up across 800 square feet. We take our time on day one.

sections.headline: Cabins and log siding
sections.text: There are a fair number of log homes and cabin-style places in the area. We handle logs, half-log siding and the decks attached to them, matching colors where we can.

sections.headline: Scheduling out north
sections.text: We group north-end jobs on the same days to keep drive time down. That helps us hold the price, and it means your neighbors may see our truck the same week.

faq.q: Do you charge more to drive out to Soddy-Daisy?
faq.a: No trip charge inside our service area. We just schedule north-end jobs together, so your start date may be tied to that week.

areas.name: East Ridge
areas.headline: Deck staining in East Ridge
areas.lede: East Ridge runs right up to the Georgia line along I-75. Lots of brick ranches with a back deck or a covered patio added on.
areas.photoAlt: Wide wood deck with a bench

sections.headline: Ranch homes, low decks
sections.text: Many East Ridge decks sit close to the ground. Low decks don't get much air underneath, so the boards stay damp longer and cup or crack. We look closely at those boards, swap out the worst ones, and choose a penetrating stain that lets the wood breathe.

sections.headline: Old solid stain that's failing
sections.text: Solid stain was popular here for a while. When it fails on a deck floor, it peels in patches and looks worse than bare wood. Stripping it is more work, so it costs more, but it's the only fix that lasts. Our calculator lets you pick 'peeling' and see the difference.

sections.headline: Quick jobs, honest quotes
sections.text: A lot of East Ridge decks are on the smaller side. Send three photos, and most of the time we can quote the job without coming out first.

faq.q: My deck has peeling solid stain. Can you just paint over it?
faq.a: We won't. Coating over a failing film just peels again, usually within a year. It has to come off first. We'll show you the price both ways so you can decide.

areas.name: East Brainerd
areas.headline: Deck staining in East Brainerd subdivisions
areas.lede: East Brainerd is subdivision country: newer homes, HOAs, and builder decks that were never stained at all.
areas.photoAlt: Close view of wood deck boards

sections.headline: The builder deck that never got stained
sections.text: The most common thing we see here: a pressure-treated deck the builder left bare. After a few summers it's gray, rough, and starting to split. It's not too late. A cleaning, a brightener, and the right stain bring most of them right back.

sections.headline: HOA colors
sections.text: If your neighborhood has an approved color list, send it to us. We'll match it, and you can try the colors on your own deck photo in our visualizer before you send the request to your HOA.

sections.headline: Same street, same week
sections.text: When we do one deck in a subdivision, two or three neighbors usually ask. If you get neighbors together for the same week, ask about a neighborhood discount.

faq.q: Can you match our HOA's approved colors?
faq.a: Yes. Send us the list or the color names, and we'll match them closely. We'll also give you a sample board to show the HOA if they need one.

areas.name: Ooltewah
areas.headline: Deck staining in Ooltewah: new decks, done right the first time
areas.lede: Ooltewah has grown fast. That means a lot of new decks, and new wood has its own rules.
areas.photoAlt: Brush applying stain to bare wood

sections.headline: Don't stain new wood too soon
sections.text: Fresh pressure-treated lumber is wet from the factory. Stain put on too early just sits on top and flakes. We use a simple water-drop test: if a few drops soak in within a few minutes, the wood is ready. If they bead up, we wait. Our article on new pressure-treated wood explains the timing.

sections.headline: …and don't wait too long
sections.text: The other mistake is leaving it bare for years. Sun turns the surface gray and loosens the fibers, and then it has to be cleaned and brightened before it will take stain well. Somewhere in that first year is the sweet spot for most decks.

sections.headline: Start a maintenance plan on day one
sections.text: A new deck is the cheapest one to keep nice. Put it on a maintenance plan after the first coat, and you may never pay for stripping.

faq.q: My deck was built this spring. When should I stain it?
faq.a: It depends on how wet the lumber was and how much sun it gets. Do the water-drop test, or send us a photo. For most new decks it's a matter of months, not years.

areas.name: Collegedale
areas.headline: Deck staining in Collegedale
areas.lede: Home to Southern Adventist University and a lot of quiet streets and family homes. The decks here are lived on.
areas.photoAlt: Porch living area with wooden chairs and plants

sections.headline: Family decks take a beating
sections.text: Grills, kiddie pools, dog paws, bikes. A deck that gets used every day wears a path. We focus extra prep on the high-traffic areas and use a stain that's easy to touch up when the time comes.

sections.headline: Rental and faculty homes
sections.text: We also work with landlords who rent near the university. A clean, stained deck helps a rental show better, and we can schedule between tenants so nobody's blocked from the back door.

sections.headline: Quiet crews
sections.text: We know these are neighborhood streets. We park neatly, keep music off, and clean up every night.

faq.q: I rent out a house in Collegedale. Can you work between tenants?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us the move-out and move-in dates and we'll fit the job in that window, weather allowing.

areas.name: Harrison
areas.headline: Deck and dock-side staining in Harrison
areas.lede: Harrison wraps around Chickamauga Lake near Harrison Bay State Park. Many homes here face the water.
areas.photoAlt: Stained wood posts and floor of an open pavilion beside trees

sections.headline: The lake is hard on wood
sections.text: Morning fog off the water, high humidity and strong afternoon sun make a rough mix for a deck finish. Stain on a waterfront deck simply works harder. We recommend a penetrating, mildew-resistant semi-transparent and an honest maintenance schedule.

sections.headline: Screened porches and gazebos
sections.text: A lot of lake homes have screened porches, gazebos or pergolas down by the water. We stain those posts, rails and floors too, and protect the screens and furniture while we work.

sections.headline: Mind the water
sections.text: When we work near the shoreline we use cleaners and methods meant for it, and we keep runoff out of the lake. Your neighbors on the cove will thank you.

woodNotes: Careful runoff control near the shoreline

faq.q: Will the stain hurt the lake or my plants?
faq.a: We use cleaners and stains suited to the job, cover plants, and control runoff. Tell us about any landscaping you're worried about and we'll plan around it.

areas.name: Apison
areas.headline: Deck, fence and barn-side staining in Apison
areas.lede: Rural east Hamilton County: acreage, horse fences, outbuildings and big decks with a view of the fields.

sections.headline: More than a deck
sections.text: Apison jobs often include a fence line, a porch, and an outbuilding or two. We'll price each piece separately so you can do it all at once or spread it over two seasons.

sections.headline: Long fence runs
sections.text: Board fences and privacy fences on acreage are a lot of linear feet. We spray and back-brush so the stain gets into the wood, not just on top of it. Just spraying looks fine for a season and then fades unevenly.

sections.headline: Out-of-the-way is fine
sections.text: Long driveway, gravel road, no cell signal? We've seen it. Send photos and a pin on the map and we'll take it from there.

faq.q: Can you stain my barn or shed too?
faq.a: Often, yes. Rough-sawn siding drinks a lot of stain, so it's priced by the wall. Send photos and we'll quote it alongside the deck.

areas.name: Fort Oglethorpe
areas.headline: Deck staining in Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia
areas.lede: Just over the state line, next to the Chickamauga battlefield park. A short run from Chattanooga for us.
areas.photoAlt: Wooden deck boards in warm light

sections.headline: Same crew, other side of the line
sections.text: Georgia customers get the same process, the same written warranty, and the same price sheet as our Tennessee customers. No surprises because of the address.

sections.headline: Older homes near the park
sections.text: Some of the older homes around the historic district and near the park have porches with decades of paint on them. We're careful with those: we test, scrape and strip only what needs to come off.

sections.headline: Newer builds off the highway
sections.text: On the newer side of town, it's mostly pressure-treated decks 5 to 15 years old. Most need a wash, brightener and two coats. Our calculator will get you close.

woodNotes: Old painted porches near the historic district

faq.q: Do you work in Georgia?
faq.a: Yes. Fort Oglethorpe, Rossville, Ringgold, Chickamauga and Dalton are all on our regular route.

areas.name: Rossville
areas.headline: Deck and porch staining in Rossville, Georgia
areas.lede: Rossville sits right below the state line, a few minutes from downtown Chattanooga. Lots of older homes with real front porches.

sections.headline: Front porches with history
sections.text: Many Rossville homes have deep front porches with tongue-and-groove floors. Those floors were made to be painted, not stained, so we'll talk with you about which finish fits. Not every job is a stain job, and we'll say so.

sections.headline: Weathered back decks
sections.text: Out back, it's usually a deck that's gone gray. Gray wood is just sun-damaged surface fibers. We wash and brighten until the clean wood shows, and then stain it.

sections.headline: Budget-friendly options
sections.text: If money's tight this year, we can do the deck floor and stairs now and the railings next season. We'll write down the plan so the colors match when we come back.

faq.q: Can you split the job over two seasons?
faq.a: Yes. Floor and stairs first, rails later is the most common split. We'll note your color and product so the second half matches.

areas.name: Chickamauga
areas.headline: Deck staining in Chickamauga, Georgia
areas.lede: A small town with farm country all around it. Decks here are often on older farmhouses or newer homes on a few acres.
areas.photoAlt: Log cabin with porch and firewood

sections.headline: Farmhouse porches and back decks
sections.text: Wraparound porches, back decks that step down to a yard, and the odd carport or pole barn. We'll look at all of it and help you decide what's worth doing first.

sections.headline: Full sun, open fields
sections.text: Out of the trees, a deck takes the full Georgia sun all afternoon. UV breaks down a finish faster than anything. A semi-transparent with good pigment holds up better than a clear, which can look great for a season and then quit.

sections.headline: Photo estimates save a trip
sections.text: It's a drive for us, so photos help. Send a wide shot of the whole deck plus a few close-ups, and you'll usually get a range before we ever come out.

woodNotes: Pigmented stain over clear for UV

faq.q: Why not a clear sealer? I like the natural look.
faq.a: Clear finishes have almost no pigment, and pigment is what blocks the sun. In full sun they wear off quickly. A light 'toner' or a semi-transparent keeps the natural look and lasts much longer.

areas.name: Ringgold
areas.headline: Deck staining in Ringgold, Georgia
areas.lede: Ringgold sits along I-75 in Catoosa County. Plenty of homes and decks here were rebuilt after the April 2011 tornado, and many of those decks are now well past their first finish.
areas.photoAlt: Freshly stained deck boards from above

sections.headline: The decks built after 2011
sections.text: When a whole area rebuilds at once, a lot of decks age on the same clock. Many of the decks put up around 2011 and 2012 got one coat, maybe two, and are now gray and checking. Good bones, tired surface. That's an easy save.

sections.headline: Newer subdivisions
sections.text: Ringgold keeps growing, and the new homes come with new pressure-treated decks. Same rule as anywhere: let new lumber dry, test it, then stain within the first year or so.

sections.headline: Fences along the property line
sections.text: Many Ringgold yards have a privacy fence that's never been sealed. Fences are vertical, so a stain lasts longer on them than on a deck floor. Doing the fence with the deck is usually a good value.

woodNotes: Decks rebuilt after 2011, now ready for refinishing

faq.q: My deck is about 13 years old and has never been stained well. Is it too far gone?
faq.a: Probably not. Unless boards are soft or cracked deep, a good cleaning and brightening brings most decks that age back. Send photos and we'll tell you.

areas.name: Dalton
areas.headline: Deck staining in Dalton, Georgia
areas.lede: Dalton is about half an hour down I-75, the edge of our regular route. We come down for full jobs and schedule them in batches.

sections.headline: How we handle the drive
sections.text: We schedule Dalton work in groups, so we're in town for a few days at a time. If you're flexible on the start date, it helps us keep the price the same as in Chattanooga.

sections.headline: Photo quotes first
sections.text: Because it's a drive, we lean on photos. Upload a wide shot of the whole deck plus a few close-ups of the worst spots. We'll give you a written range before anyone gets in the truck.

sections.headline: Bigger lots, bigger decks
sections.text: Many Dalton-area homes sit on larger lots with long decks and a fence to match. If you're doing both, book them together so it's one trip, one setup.

woodNotes: Batched scheduling on the edge of our route

faq.q: Is there a travel charge for Dalton?
faq.a: No separate trip charge for full jobs. Very small jobs may need to wait until we have other work in the area.

areas.name: Cleveland
areas.headline: Deck staining in Cleveland, Tennessee
areas.lede: Cleveland is about 30 miles up I-75 in Bradley County. We serve it with planned trips and photo estimates.
areas.photoAlt: Deck with wooden railing and chairs

sections.headline: A growing town, lots of newer decks
sections.text: Cleveland has grown a lot, and the newer subdivisions are full of pressure-treated decks that were never finished. Catch them in the first few years and they stay easy and cheap to keep up.

sections.headline: Lake and mountain weekends
sections.text: Many Cleveland families also have a weekend place toward the Ocoee or up on a lake. If you've got two decks, we'll quote both and schedule them back to back.

sections.headline: Planned trips
sections.text: We group Bradley County jobs together. Get your photos in early in the season to get a good slot, especially for fall.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book in Cleveland?
faq.a: For fall, the best staining season, book by late summer. Spring has more open dates.

articles.title: The best time to stain a deck in {city}
articles.description: Why {bestMonths} are the best months to stain a deck in {city}, with NOAA rainfall numbers and what the wood needs to dry.
goDeeper: [How much stain will my deck need?](source:supplierCalculator) (Stain & Seal Supply)

body.lede: Short answer: **{bestMonths}**. Spring is our second choice. Midsummer and winter are the hardest. Here's why.

body.h2: Stain needs dry wood and a few dry days

body: Stain has to soak into the wood. If the boards are wet, it can't. The U.S. Forest Products Laboratory, the government's wood research lab, says to let a deck dry for at least two warm, windy days after cleaning before you finish it{cite:usdaFinishes}. Home Depot's guide for pressure-treated wood says to let it dry 24 hours after cleaning{cite:homeDepot}. On a shady deck in a humid valley, we lean toward the longer number.
So the real question is: *when does {city} give you a run of dry days?*
{city} averages about **{annualRain} inches of rain a year**. The driest months on average are {driestMonths}, and {fewestRainDays} have the fewest rainy days{cite:climate}.

That lines up with what we see on the job. Fall gives us dry spells, cooler afternoons and less direct heat on the boards. Stain that goes on in mild weather soaks in evenly instead of flashing dry on the surface.

July is one of the wettest months here on average, and pop-up afternoon storms are common. Hot boards also dry the stain too fast, which leaves lap marks. We still work in summer, but we start early, work in the shade side first, and watch the radar.

Most stains need air and wood temperatures above about 50°F while they dry. Check the label of the product you're using. Winter days are short and the boards stay damp in the morning. We use winter for estimates and booking.
Average humidity here is {humidity}{cite:humidity}. Humidity slows drying, which is one more reason we don't rush the wait between washing and staining.

checklist: Book early for {bestMonths}. Those slots fill first.
Spring works well too once the pollen settles.
If your deck is peeling or gray now, get it on the calendar. Waiting another season usually means more prep and a bigger bill.

articles.title: Oil vs. water-based deck stain: the honest answer
articles.description: Oil-based and water-based deck stains compared in plain English: how long they last, how they wear, and which is easier to redo.
goDeeper: [Why penetrating oil stains protect wood differently](source:expertPenetrating) (EXPERT)

body.lede: You'll hear strong opinions on this. The truth is the experts don't fully agree, and the "right" answer depends on how you want to take care of the deck later.

body: Fine Homebuilding says most water-based stains actually *last longer* than oil-based ones, about two to three years. The catch is that when they do wear out, you often have to remove the old coat completely before recoating. Oil-based stains need refinishing more often, but the touch-up is easier{cite:fineHomebuilding}.
Bob Vila's cost guide puts it the other way, with oil-based lasting about 3 to 5 years and water-based about 2 to 3{cite:bobvila}.
Both are reputable. The difference comes from the products tested, the climate, and how "lasting" gets measured. That's why we don't sell one answer to everybody.

body.h2: How they wear, in plain words

compare.title: Oil-based
items: Soaks deep into the wood and brings out the grain
Wears away slowly. It fades more than it peels.
Easy to recoat: clean it and add a coat where it's thin{cite:fineHomebuilding}
Stronger smell, slower to dry, harder cleanup

compare.title: Water-based
items: Holds its color well and dries fast
Low odor and easy cleanup
Can last longer between coats{cite:fineHomebuilding}
When it's done, it may need to be stripped first

body: For most decks around {city}, we like a **penetrating, semi-transparent** stain, oil or a modern water-based "hybrid," and a maintenance coat every couple of years. The Forest Products Lab recommends penetrating finishes over film-forming ones for decks{cite:usdaFinishes}. If you want to keep the cost of upkeep low, choose the product that's easiest to recoat. That way your second coat in three years is a quick wash-and-stain, not a strip job.

body.h2: Already have a finish on there?

body: Stay with the same type if it's in good shape. Putting water-based over oil, or oil over a film that's still on the wood, is a common reason a new coat fails. When we're not sure what's on a deck, we test a spot first.

articles.title: Semi-transparent vs. solid stain on a deck
articles.description: The government wood lab says avoid solid stain on decks. Consumer Reports says solid scores best. Here is how to decide.

body.lede: This is the one question where two trusted sources give opposite advice. We'll show you both and tell you how we decide on the job.

body: The U.S. Forest Products Laboratory has studied wood finishes for decades. Their advice for decks is clear: use **penetrating** finishes, not film-forming ones. They write that paints and solid-color stains "are prone to trap moisture and fail by peeling"{cite:usdaFinishes}. Another of their guides says paint and solid-color stains "are not appropriate for fully exposed decks"{cite:usdaSouth}, and a third says opaque stains shouldn't be used on decks and fences{cite:usdaFinishing}.
Their own table gives semi-transparent stain on decking about 2–3 years on new smooth wood and 3–6 years on weathered, rougher wood{cite:usdaSouth}.

Consumer Reports tests deck stains on panels outdoors. Their tester told KOMO News that "solid color staining always fares best in our testing," and that a solid color can last seven to 10 years, while clearer stains may need redoing every one to three years{cite:consumerReports}.

They're measuring different things. Consumer Reports rates how the finish *looks and protects* over time on test panels. The Forest Products Lab focuses on how the finish *fails* on a real deck, where water gets in at the board ends, cracks and nail holes. When a solid stain does fail on a floor, it peels, and peeling means stripping. When a semi-transparent wears, it fades, and fading means a quick recoat.

compare.title: We lean semi-transparent when…
items: It's a walking surface: deck floors, stairs
The deck is shady or damp (think {shadyArea})
You want to see the wood grain
You want cheap, easy maintenance coats

compare.title: Solid can make sense when…
items: It's vertical: railings, skirting, fences, siding
The wood is mismatched or patched and you want one even color
You understand a failed solid coat means stripping later
There's good airflow and drainage

body: A popular middle path: **semi-transparent on the floor, solid on the railings.** You get a grain look underfoot and a crisp, long-lasting color on the parts you look at most.
Our written warranty reflects this. Solid stain on deck floors gets a shorter term, and we tell you why up front.

articles.title: New pressure-treated deck? When to stain it
articles.description: How long to wait before staining a new pressure-treated deck, the 10-minute sprinkle test, and why waiting too long costs you.
goDeeper: [The lifecycle of exterior wood: from new construction on](source:expertLifecycle) (EXPERT)

body.lede: Brand-new deck? Don't stain it the day the builder leaves, and don't wait three years either.

body: Pressure-treated lumber comes from the yard wet. Home Depot's guide says it can take several weeks to dry{cite:homeDepot}. Stain put on wet wood can't soak in. It sits on top and flakes off.
The Forest Products Lab's deck guide says wood that was treated with a water repellent at the factory, or recently treated, should weather for about 2 to 3 months before finishing{cite:usdaFinishes}.

steps: Sprinkle some water on a few boards in the sun and a few in the shade.
If it soaks in, the wood is ready. Plan to stain soon. If it beads up or pools, give it more time{cite:homeDepot}.

body: One exception: lumber stamped **KDAT** (kiln dried after treatment) has already been dried and can be stained right away{cite:homeDepot}.

body.h2: Why you don't wait too long

body: Bare wood in the sun turns gray within a season or two. That gray layer is damaged surface fiber. Stain won't stick well to it until it's cleaned and brightened, which adds a step and cost. The Forest Products Lab notes that most decks are retired early because of cracks and checks that timely finishing could have prevented{cite:usdaFinishes}.

body.h2: Our advice for a new deck

checklist: Do the sprinkle test every few weeks after the deck is built.
When it passes, book the first coat. For most decks that's within the first year.
Ask about a maintenance plan. A new deck is the cheapest one to keep looking new.

articles.title: Why deck stain peels (and how to stop it)
articles.description: The real reasons deck stain peels: film finishes, wet wood, and coating over old finish. Plus what fixes it for good.
goDeeper: [Why penetrating oil stains protect wood differently](source:expertPenetrating) (EXPERT)
[EXPERT Clean & Bright: cleaners, brighteners and strippers](source:expertCleanBright)

body.lede: Peeling is the number one complaint we hear. It's almost never bad luck. There are a few causes, and they're all fixable.

body.h2: 1. A film finish on a walking surface

body: Paints and solid stains form a film on top of the wood. The Forest Products Lab says film-forming finishes on decks are prone to trap moisture and fail by peeling{cite:usdaFinishes}. Semi-transparent stains, by comparison, won't blister or peel even if water gets into the wood{cite:usdaFinishes}. They fade instead.

Stain on damp wood can't grip. That happens when someone stains the day after a rain, the morning after washing, or on brand-new lumber that hasn't dried. The lab recommends at least two warm, windy days of drying after cleaning{cite:usdaFinishes}.

body.h2: 3. New coat on top of a failing coat

body: If the old finish is lifting, a new coat on top is only as strong as what's underneath. It peels right along with it. This is the most common mistake we fix.
More isn't better. Penetrating stain should soak in. The extra that sits in puddles on top dries into a soft film that scuffs and flakes. We back-brush and wipe off any excess before it dries.

A high-pressure wash can tear up soft wood. The lab warns that aggressive scrubbing or power washing can remove wood from the surface{cite:usdaFinishes}. That fuzzy surface takes stain unevenly. We wash with low pressure and the right cleaner, and let the chemistry do the work.

steps: Strip what's failing, all of it, down to sound wood.
Brighten the wood so it's open and even.
Apply a penetrating stain and back-brush it in.
Recoat on schedule, before it wears through.

body: Stripping is the most work we do, so a peeling deck costs more than one that's just faded. Our [price calculator](/pricing/) shows the difference when you choose "Peeling."

articles.title: How often to restain a deck in {stateName} humidity
articles.description: How many years a deck stain really lasts in {stateName}: what Angi, Bob Vila and the U.S. Forest Products Lab say, and what changes it.
goDeeper: [What to look for in a professional-grade wood stain](source:expertProGrade) (EXPERT)

body.lede: Most decks around here want attention every **two to three years**. Railings and fences can usually go longer. Here's what the sources say, and what moves the number up or down.

head: Source
What they say
rows: Restain every two to three years
Semi-transparent on decking: 2–3 years on new smooth wood, 3–6 years on weathered rough wood
Clear water-repellent sealers: about 1 year on exposed deck surfaces

body: Those are averages. The lab's own table says its numbers are for an average location in the continental United States{cite:usdaSouth}. {city} isn't average.

We get about {annualRain} inches of rain a year here{cite:climate}, and average humidity is {humidity}{cite:humidity}. Wet wood that dries slowly grows mildew, and mildew breaks down a finish from the top. Add strong summer sun on open decks and you get wear from both sides.

body.h2: What makes yours last longer or shorter

compare.title: Shorter
items: Full afternoon sun on the deck floor
Heavy shade and leaf piles
Clear or very light finishes (less pigment, less UV protection)
Dogs, grills, planters, kids

compare.title: Longer
items: Vertical surfaces: railings, fences, siding
Good airflow under and around the deck
Semi-transparent with good pigment
A yearly wash and a quick check

body.h2: The cheapest way to keep a deck nice

body: Recoat *before* it wears through. A maintenance coat on a faded deck costs a fraction of stripping a failed one. That's the whole idea behind our [maintenance plans](/services/maintenance-plans/), and why our dashboard reminds us to call you before your deck needs it.
And check the structure while you're at it. The North American Deck and Railing Association recommends homeowners check their deck every year{cite:nadra}.
